chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, and others, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ibn Baqqah, from Al-Hakam ibn Ayman, from Abu Asama Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever has forty days pass by him and he does not eat meat, then let him borrow upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and let him eat it.'

key_terms.يَسْتَقْرِضْ: Let him borrow (metaphorically asking Allah for provision)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on not eating meat for forty days in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the physical and spiritual impact of dietary consistency, suggesting that a forty-day meat fast alters one's mannerisms, necessitating a return to meat consumption. The phrase 'borrow upon Allah' (istaqrid) reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of divine provision, implying that the body has a right to specific nourishment which Allah guarantees to restore balance. This practice underscores the importance of maintaining bodily health as a prerequisite for spiritual devotion in Shia tradition.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, and someone else, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ibn Baqqah, from Al Hakam Bin Ayman, from Abu Asama Zayd Al Shahaam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one to whom forty days come by and he does not eat the meat, so let him borrow upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic and let him eat it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar and others from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn Ali from ibn Baqqah from al- Hakam ibn Ayman from abu ‘Usamah Zayd al-Shahham who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘One with whom forty days pass and has not eaten meat should borrow, on the credit of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, to buy meat to eat.’”
